raised.claim: Verdicts attached to new issues are never checked against the proposed issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A zero-candidate row can reference a new issue whose scope is candidates_count > 0 with no enumerated beer_ids; the issue is created and the row is linked despite contradicting that scope, whereas the identical attachment to an existing issue is rejected.

raised.claim: Adding any enumerated beer_id bypasses the prohibition on whole-class where scopes.
raised.why_it_breaks: The normal model output can include beer_ids: [1] alongside where: [{col: 'review_class', op: '=', value: 'matcher_bug'}]. This passes legality, but rowSatisfiesScope treats the cohort and predicate as alternatives, so every future matcher_bug row satisfies it and the whole-class dumping-ground scope survives.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not account for rows already accepted in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: With postCreationRows equal to 11, a batch containing 50 matching verdicts for the same issue passes this unchanged check 50 times and posts all of them, growing the issue to 61 post-creation rows despite the limit of 12.

raised.claim: A scope block in the model-authored issue body takes precedence over the authoritative rendered scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If issue.body contains a valid ```triage-scope block, it appears before the block appended here. BLOCK_RE takes the first match, so the next run enforces the model-authored block rather than issue.scope; an earlier malformed block can instead make the issue permanently unscoped. Escaping contains values does not protect this separate prose field.

raised.claim: Guard counters are omitted whenever the model supplies a verdict for every row, even if guards reject every verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a complete 50-row response routed to an unscoped or saturated issue, covered remains 50 because it is computed from analysis.verdicts before guard filtering. This branch never logs guardHits, so the repeated rejection loop that the new logging is intended to expose remains invisible.

raised.claim: An empty probe is accepted as absence evidence even when the other probe returns hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a brewery-label error, the brewery-only probe can return '' while the name-only probe finds the actual beer under its correct brewery. A not_on_untappd verdict still passes this OR condition and blocks the paid fallback despite the conflicting positive evidence. The reverse combination also passes.

raised.claim: The new absence-degradation path causes matcher_bug verdicts to be reported as wontfix in the daily outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: A not_on_untappd verdict without a probe is now added to plan.quiet as matcher_bug. The job's quiet execution loop increments outcome.wontfix for every class other than not_on_untappd, so this newly introduced path displays a wontfix count although the persisted class is matcher_bug and the beer remains retryable.

raised.claim: The timestamp comparison uses lexicographic ordering across different ISO timestamp precisions.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub supplies created_at with second precision, such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z, while review timestamps use toISOString(), such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z. The latter is chronologically later but compares smaller as TEXT because '.' sorts before 'Z', so a post-creation attachment in the same second is not counted.

raised.claim: The new authoritative issue link is not cleared when a failure is reopened for triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: After this setter attaches a row to issue 347, recordEnrichFailure can cross the zero/nonzero candidate boundary and clear review_class, review_note and reviewed_at, but it leaves issue_number equal to 347. The reopened, unreviewed row therefore retains an authoritative link to its old issue even though its classification and supporting routing note have been invalidated.

raised.quote:
export const V23_BACKFILL_SQL = `
  UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The backfill extracts the first arrow reference rather than the appended routing suffix.
raised.why_it_breaks: A model-authored review_note can already contain an arrow reference, for example 'related pattern → #228', before the job appends the actual routing suffix ' → #347'. The migration assigns issue_number 228 rather than 347, corrupting the authoritative link and attributing saturation counts to the wrong issue.
